1.  Present application is filed by the applicants who are  husband's in-laws for quashing of First Information Report in  connection with Crime No.111/2020, registered with Police  Station Nandura, under Sections 498A, 307, 323, 504 and 506  read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

T  crime was registered against the present applicants on the basis  of report lodged by the respondent No.2 on an allegations that  her marriage was performed with applicant No.1 and after  marriage she resumed cohabitation at her matrimonial house,
 but she was not treated well and she was ill-treated for various  reasons including for the unlawful demands.
She furt  alleged that the present applicants also attempted to commit  her murder.
On the basis of the said report Police have  registered the crime against the present applicants.
2. During the pendency of the application both arrived  938-apl491.20.odt 2/4  at a settlement.
Both are present before the Court.
The  contents of settlement are verified from them, as far as the  offence under Section 307 is concerned.

On perusal of the  investigation papers it reveals that there is no such medical  certificate on record to show that there was any attempt by the Rishikesh Gajanan Unhale And 3 Others vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. Pso Ps ... on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156795834/
1  present applicants to strangulate her.

sentences.text: 3. In view of settlement they have already obtained the  decree of dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.

The  affidavit is also filed by the respondent No.2 contending that  now she has no grievance against the present applicants and  they have decided to withdraw all the litigations pending  between them including the present application.
In view of  that, applicants prayed for quashing of the First Information  Report.

4. Heard learned counsel for the applicants and  learned A.P.P. for the respondent No.1/State as well as learned  counsel for the respondent No.2.
 5.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in  the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another,
 reported in MANU/SC/0781/2012, wherein the Hon'ble Apex  Court observed that "Where the High Court quashes a criminal  proceeding having regard to the fact that the dispute between  the offender and victim has been settled, although the offences  are not compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation  of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice  in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is put  to an end and peace is restored; securing the ends of justice  being the ultimate guiding factor."
 6.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this regard a specific reference was made to the  938-apl491.20.odt 3/4  offences arising out of matrimony, particularly relating to  dowry, etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong is basically  to victim but the offender and victim have settled all disputes  between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that such  offences have not been made compoundable.
In recent  Judgment in Naushey Ali and others Vs. State of U.P. and  another, reported in (2025)4 SCC 78 wherein also the Hon'ble  Court observed that when parties have amicably resolved

entities.text: Naushey Ali and others Vs. State of U.P. and  another, reported in (2025)4 SCC 78
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the  dispute would be futile and the ends of justice require that the  settlement be given effect to by quashing the proceedings.
It  would be a grave abuse of process particularly when dispute is  settled and resolved.

7. In view of the above observations of the Hon'ble  Apex Court here in the present application also the dispute  between the parties of a matrimonial nature and no purpose  would be served by forcing the applicants to face the trial.

As  far as the offence punishable under Section 307 is concerned  which is not made out from the recitals of the F.I.R. and the  entire investigation papers.
 8.
However, the entire Police machinery and Court  machinery is used and they have to spare their time for  investigation and for the trial.
In view of that, the application  deserves to be allowed.

Hence, we proceed to pass following  order :
 ORDER Rishikesh Gajanan Unhale And 3 Others vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. Pso Ps ... on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156795834/
2 (i) The application is allowed, subject to payment of costs of Rs.20,000/- by the applicants be paid to the High Court Bar Association, Nagpur and Rs.20,000/- by the respondent No.2 be paid to the High Court Legal Services Sub-Committee, Nagpur.
(ii) The First Information Report in connection with Crime No.111/2020, registered with Police Station Nandura, under Sections 498A, 307, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing Sessions Case No.46/2021 is hereby quashed and set aside.
